@ the time and a parameter at sample / 4 in an expression: the time of the tick, kept for its four frames
@ the same in two lets, the name of the parameter and the sum
@ the same as the argument of a call of a function
@ a tick of sample / 2: the ticks at the frames 0 2 4 6 read 0 2 4 6, p = 1
@ the parameter changes with the call and the value of the tick is made again: p = 0 and p = 4
@ the sum is kept where the host cuts the run in the middle of a tick
@ the time and the parameter in a condition of && and the let that holds it: 1 for the frames of the ticks 4 and 12
@ the remainder of the sum: p = 0 holds at the ticks 4 and 12, p = 4 at the ticks 0 and 8
@ a parameter at a tick alone, with no time in it, is read where it is: its value at each frame
@ a tick of sample / 8: the ticks at the frames 0 and 8 read 0 and 8, p = 1
@ with a sample input the sum is the value of its tick for the four frames, added to the input of each frame
@ the parameter in a branch of an if the time chooses: the value of the tick where the time is 4 or 12 (12 mod 8 is 4), else 0
@ the parameter compared in a let, with the time: p = 3 holds at the ticks 4 and 12, p = 2 never
@ the sum with the clock of the time written (`sample_tick() at (sample / 4)`) is the same value as the sum without it
